result.rationale: The mechanism is verifiable in the diff: addGuests.handler.ts authorizes any attendee of a booking (isAttendee check) to add guests, and each call triggers sendAddGuestsEmails (email-manager.ts) which pushes emails to the organizer, every team member, and every attendee, sent from the organizer's mailer identity with replyTo set to organizer and all attendee emails. Repeated guest additions by an attendee thus relay bulk email attributed to the organizer with no rate limiting, a real spam/spoofing surface introduced by this change. Whether maintainers consider it acceptable design is uncertain

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation explicitly allows any existing attendee to add arbitrary guest emails (`const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find(...);` and the permission check only forbids when `!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee`). After adding, it always calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which sends emails to the organizer (and team members) plus *every* attendee (`calendarEvent.attendees.map(...)`), meaning an attendee can trigger emails to many third-party addresses by submitting a large `guests` list (no rate/size limits shown in the diff). The finding’s “spoofed from organizer” aspect is somewhat overstated, but attendee-driven mass email sending/spam relay is directly enabled by the diff.
